Accused Nos. 1 to 7 in Crime No.117/2023 registered by Mandya West Police Station, Mandya, for the offences punishable under Section 406, 420, 465, 468, 471, 201, 120B, NC: 2023:KHC:41405 114 and 149 of IPC, are before this Court in these two petitions filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
2.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. On the basis of the typed complaint dated 17.08.2023 lodged by the Chief Executive Officer of Vishwagnani Employees Development Co-operative Society, Mandya, the Station House Officer of Mandya West Police Station, has registered FIR in Crime No.117/2023 against the petitioners herein for the aforesaid offences.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. Accused No.1 is the ex-president of the complainant Society and accused No.2 is the ex-secretary of complainant society.
Accused Nos.3 to 7 are said to be the employees of the Society and also relatives of accused No.1.

Apprehending arrest in the said case, accused Nos.1 to 7/petitioners had filed Crl. Misc. No.751/2023 before the Court of IV Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Mandya,
which was dismissed on 22.09.2023.

entities.text: Court of IV Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Mandya
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, they are before this Court.

5. Learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that at the behest of the present NC: 2023:KHC:41405 management of the Society, the CEO of the Society has filed a false complaint against the ex-president, ex-secretary and other employees of the Society.

He submits that on the allegation of misappropriation in the Society during the term of first accused, enquiry is being held under Section 64 of the Karnataka Co-Operative Societies Act and the said enquiry is still pending.
The said enquiry is initiated based on the complaint made by the henchmen of the present president.
Being unsuccessful to get an order in the said proceedings, a false police complaint is lodged only with an intention to harass and coerce the earlier management of the Society.
He submits that accused Nos.3 to 7 have been granted interim bail by this Court and they have not violated the bail conditions.
He also submits that the petitioners are ready and willing to co-operate with the investigating officer for the purpose of investigation.
He submits that the first accused has demitted his office in the year 2021 and in the year 2021, there is an Audit Report filed prior to the first petitioner demitting his office.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

6. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the bail petition and submits that serious charges of misappropriation NC: 2023:KHC:41405 are made against the accused persons and therefore,
custodial interrogation of accused persons is necessary.
7. Learned counsel for respondent No.2/defecto complainant has also opposed the bail petition.
She submits that accused persons have threatened the complainant and other material witnesses in the case.
In that regard, she has filed an affidavit of the complainant.
She also submits that first accused was involved in similar criminal cases and number of cases have been registered against him.

Accordingly, she prays to dismiss the petition.
8.

FIR in Crime No.117/2023 has been registered by Mandya West Police Station, Mandya, against the petitioners herein based on the complaint of the CEO of the Society, of which accused No.1 is the Past-President and accused No.2 is the Past-Secretary.

The allegations in the complaint is that Sri Surendra vs State By Mandya West on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104018911/
4 during the term of accused persons, there has been misappropriation and the accused persons by misusing their power have caused financial loss to the Society.

sentences.text: The material made available to the Court by learned Senior counsel for the petitioners would go to show that after the first petitioner had NC: 2023:KHC:41405 demitted his office in the year 2021, on the basis of complaint made by one Sri. Nagaraj, the competent authority has initiated proceedings under Section 64 of the Karnataka Co- Operative Societies Act and proceedings in the said case is still pending.
Even before a Report is submitted in the said proceedings, a separate police complaint is filed on the allegation of misappropriation by the erstwhile management of the Society.

The provisions of the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, provides for a mechanism for the purpose of adjudicating the allegations and complaints made with regard to mismanagement and misappropriation in the Society and in the present case, already an enquiry under Section 64 of the Societies Act has been initiated against the earlier management of the Society.

9. Though learned counsel for respondent No.2 has submitted that there are number of criminal cases pending against accused No.1 and he has cheated many other managements, she has not produced any material in support of the said contention of hers.
From a reading of the complaint averment, it is seen that allegation against the petitioners is about mismanagement and misappropriation of the funds of the Society.
The said allegations are principally based on documentary evidence and entire documents relating to the case are in the custody of present management and the complainant.
Therefore, the apprehension put-forth by the complainant that the petitioners are trying to tamper with the evidence is ill-founded.
The complainant has stated that the petitioners have threatened the complainant.
Except the affidavit filed by the complainant, there is no material to show that the petitioners herein have threatened the complainant or other witnesses.
Complainant has not filed any police complaint against the petitioners with regard to the alleged threat by them.
The offences alleged against the petitioners are all triable by the Court of Magistrate and the maximum punishment for the alleged offence is imprisonment by seven years.
Accused Nos.3 to 7/petitioners in Crl.P.No.9801/2023 have been granted interim bail and there is no complaint that they have misused the order of interim bail granted to them.
Learned Senior counsel has submitted that the petitioners are ready and willing to co-operate with the investigation officer.
Under the circumstances, I am of the view that the petitioners have made out a case for grant of anticipatory bail.
12. Accordingly, the petitions are allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioners in the event of their arrest in Crime No.117/2023 registered by Mandya West Police Station, Mandya, for the offence punishable under Section 406,
